question: When an install fact changes — a marketplace name, a package name, a plugin path — what makes the READMEs follow?

options.label: Hand-written prose, with a test that reads the manifests and fails when they disagree
options.reason: The prose stays editable by anyone in any editor, and the facts that actually break a user's install — marketplace name, plugin path, package name, link targets — are pinned by something that runs in CI. It matches how the repository already treats correctness: plugin.test.ts asserts the generated skills match their source rather than trusting them.
options.costLater: The check only catches what it was told to look for. Prose that goes stale in a way the assertions do not cover — a step that no longer exists, an option that was renamed — still ships, and every new install fact needs someone to remember to extend the check.

options.label: Generated from plugins/hosts/*.json through scripts/build-plugins.mjs
options.reason: One source of truth, mechanically enforced, and the host JSON already exists as the place per-host facts live. Drift becomes impossible rather than detectable.
options.costLater: Every wording change becomes a code change plus a regenerated diff, and the generator has to grow a templating layer it does not have today. Documentation quality then depends on how expressive that template is, which is the usual way generated prose ends up sounding generated.

options.label: Hand-written, checked by nobody
options.reason: Cheapest now and honest about scale: four host READMEs and one root README are few enough that a human reviewing a PR can see when one is wrong. It is what the repository does today.
options.costLater: It is also what produced the thing being fixed here — three READMEs telling people to clone a repository that one of them does not need cloned, and a Hosts table linking to a README that was never written. The same drift recurs the next time a host is added.
